next_best:
Continue working on this project. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 0 — orient (run these first, read the output):
  git status && git log --oneline -5

Step 1 — pick the highest-impact task by scanning in order:
  (1) interrupted/uncommitted work to resume
  (2) failing tests, broken builds, or type errors
  (3) SSOT/DRY/quality violations flagged in code or session
  (4) mission alignment — are we building the right things?

Step 2 — execute it fully. No questions, no scope creep, no partial work.

Step 3 — verify before marking done:
  • Run type checker if one exists: tsc --noEmit OR mypy OR cargo check
  • Run tests if suite exists: npm test OR pytest OR cargo test
  • Count TODOs: grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME\|HACK' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.py' --include='*.go' | wc -l
  • Check git status — are changes committed or intentionally staged?

Step 4 — update the session file with VERIFIED data (not guesses):
done: <one sentence>
next: <one sentence>
tests: <run them — N pass · N fail, or 'no suite'>
todos: <actual grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
build: <clean | N type errors | skipped — no checker found>
test_and_fix:
Run the full test suite and fix every failure. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — detect and run the test suite:
  Try in order: npm test, pytest, cargo test, go test ./...
  If none found: write tests for the 2 most critical untested paths.

Step 2 — for each failure: read the error, find the root cause, fix it. Never mock away a real problem.

Step 3 — start the dev server and use browser automation (mcp__playwright or mcp__claude-in-chrome) to walk primary user flows. Check browser console for errors. Fix every bug found.

Step 4 — run type checker to zero errors: tsc --noEmit OR mypy OR cargo check.

Step 5 — update session file:
done: <what you fixed>
next: <what remains>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
build: <clean | N type errors>
browser: <N/M flows passing | untested>
browser_test:
Test this application in a real browser using mcp__playwright or mcp__claude-in-chrome tools.

Step 1 — start the dev server if not running.

Step 2 — test each primary user flow systematically:
  • App loads without console errors
  • Primary create/read/update/delete flows
  • Authentication flow (if applicable)
  • Mobile viewport at 375px width
  • Empty states and error states
  Read browser console after each flow — fix every error.

Step 3 — fix every bug found before moving on.

Step 4 — update session file:
done: <what you tested and fixed>
next: <remaining issues or untested flows>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
browser: <N/M flows passing — list any failures>
quality:
Code health pass — raise the bar, no new features. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — run automated checks:
  • Type checker: tsc --noEmit OR mypy OR cargo check
  • Linter: npm run lint OR flake8 OR clippy
  • Count TODOs: grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME\|HACK' src/ (or equivalent)

Step 2 — fix all type/lint errors.

Step 3 — search for and fix:
  • DRY violations (same logic in 2+ places → extract)
  • SSOT gaps (same data defined in multiple files → centralize)
  • Magic numbers/strings → constants
  • Copy-paste code blocks → shared utilities
  • TODO debt older than 2 sessions → resolve or delete
  • Files over 300 lines → split if they have multiple concerns

Step 4 — update session file:
done: <what you cleaned up>
next: <remaining debt>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <actual grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
build: <clean | N errors after your fixes>
commit_push:
Prepare and ship today's work. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — verify (must pass before committing):
  • Type check: tsc --noEmit OR equivalent — zero errors required
  • Tests: must pass
  • No console.log in production paths
  • No hardcoded secrets or API keys

Step 2 — review changes:
  git diff && git status
  Stage only intentional changes.

Step 3 — commit with conventional format:
  <type>(<scope>): <description that explains WHY>
  Types: feat, fix, refactor, perf, test, docs, chore

Step 4 — push to origin.

Step 5 — if Vercel project, monitor deployment until Ready:
  vercel ls --prod (poll until status = Ready or Error)
  If Error: run vercel logs <url>, fix, push again.

Step 6 — update session file:
done: committed and pushed — <commit message>
next: <next priority>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
build: <clean | N errors>
deploy: <https://... Ready | local only>
deploy_check:
Full pre-deploy verification. Fix every issue found. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Run each check and report pass/fail:
  (1) Type check — tsc --noEmit or equivalent: ZERO errors
  (2) Build — npm run build or equivalent: must complete without error
  (3) Tests — all passing
  (4) No console.log or debug code in production paths
  (5) No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials (grep for common patterns)
  (6) All user-facing API routes have input validation
  (7) No incomplete features without proper guards/feature flags
  (8) Security: SQL injection, XSS, auth bypass — check critical paths
  (9) Performance: no N+1 queries, no blocking operations on main thread

Fix every failure. Only when ALL 9 checks pass: commit, push, monitor deployment.

Update session file:
done: <pre-deploy checks result + deployed if clean>
next: <any items that need attention post-deploy>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
build: <clean | N errors>
deploy: <https://... Ready | failed — see logs>
full_audit:
Comprehensive project audit. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Phase 1 — gather hard data (run all of these):
  • git log --oneline -20 (what shipped recently?)
  • git status (uncommitted work?)
  • tsc --noEmit OR equivalent (type errors?)
  • npm test OR pytest OR equivalent (test health?)
  • grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME\|HACK' src/ | wc -l (debt count?)
  • wc -l $(find src -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' -o -name '*.py' 2>/dev/null) | sort -rn | head -10 (largest files)

Phase 2 — audit dimensions:
  • Architecture: are concerns properly separated? Any god files/components?
  • SSOT: is any data defined in multiple places?
  • DRY: any obvious copy-paste?
  • Security: any obvious vulnerabilities at system boundaries?
  • Missing tests: what critical paths have no coverage?
  • Mission drift: do recent commits match the stated purpose?

Phase 3 — write a priority list (5 items, by user impact).

Phase 4 — execute the single highest-priority item fully.

Update session file:
done: <what you fixed>
next: <top remaining item from priority list>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <actual grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
build: <clean | N type errors>
mission:
Define and align the project mission. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — read CLAUDE.md (if exists) and extract the stated mission.
  If no mission: draft one — answer these 3 questions in 2 sentences:
    Who is the actual user? What problem do they have? What does success look like?
  Prepend to CLAUDE.md under a '## Mission' heading.

Step 2 — audit last 10 commits: git log --oneline -10
  Are we building the right things?
  Is anything over-engineered, gold-plated, or solving a problem nobody has?
  Is anything critically missing for the user to get value?

Step 3 — fix the single biggest misalignment.

Step 4 — write a one-line value proposition (outcome-focused, no jargon, under 12 words).

Update session file:
done: <what you realigned or defined>
next: <next misalignment to address>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
mission: <one-line value proposition you wrote>
product:
Think as a product manager. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — gather context:
  • Read CLAUDE.md for stated mission
  • git log --oneline -10 (what was built recently?)
  • Check if there's a MARKETING.md or README with value proposition

Step 2 — answer these 4 questions honestly:
  (1) Who is the actual user and what is their single biggest pain point RIGHT NOW?
  (2) What is the most confusing part of the current UX — would a new user understand in 30 seconds?
  (3) What one feature would have the highest impact if shipped this week?
  (4) What should be CUT — features that add complexity without proportional user value?

Step 3 — produce a prioritized list of 5 improvements with user-impact rationale.

Step 4 — execute the single highest-impact UX fix.

Update session file:
done: <product insight + fix applied>
next: <next highest-impact improvement>
tests: <N pass · N fail>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
ux: <key finding — one sentence>
ux_review:
Review the UI/UX as a demanding but fair user. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — start dev server and open in browser (use mcp__playwright or mcp__claude-in-chrome).

Step 2 — systematically check each dimension and RECORD specific file:line issues:
  Typography: all text ≥14px? No gray-on-gray? Readable everywhere?
  Interactivity: buttons/links/inputs obviously clickable? Hover states?
  Mobile: 375px viewport — does it work? Tap targets ≥44px?
  Empty states: what does the user see with no data? Is there a helpful message?
  Loading states: are async operations shown clearly?
  Error states: are error messages helpful and actionable (not 'Something went wrong')?
  Visual hierarchy: is the most important action the most prominent element?
  Consistency: same patterns used for same things throughout?

Step 3 — fix the top 3 issues found. Reference file:line for each fix.

Step 4 — update session file:
done: <UX issues found and fixed>
next: <remaining UX issues>
tests: <flows passing in browser>
todos: <grep count> TODOs
health: <good | needs attention | critical>
browser: <N/M flows tested — key findings>
ux: <summary: N issues found, M fixed — worst remaining issue>
marketing:
Write compelling marketing copy. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — read CLAUDE.md mission section and recent git log for what was built.

Step 2 — create all of the following (save to MARKETING.md):
  (1) One-line value proposition — under 12 words, outcome-focused, no jargon
      Example: 'Ship better software faster without breaking things'
  (2) Three-sentence elevator pitch — problem → solution → why this one
  (3) Three feature bullets — written as user benefits ('You can...' not 'It has...')
  (4) One call-to-action line
  (5) Three potential objections and honest answers
  (6) Target user persona — 2 sentences: who they are, what they struggle with

Step 3 — review: would a skeptical stranger be convinced?
  Cut jargon. Focus on outcomes. Make it human.

Update session file:
done: wrote marketing copy to MARKETING.md
next: review copy with fresh eyes and refine the weakest section
tests: n/a
todos: 0
health: good
mission: <the one-line value proposition you wrote>
social:
Write authentic social media content based on recent work. Follow CLAUDE.md.

Step 1 — check git log for the last week: git log --since='7 days ago' --oneline
  Identify the most concrete, impressive, or interesting thing that shipped.

Step 2 — write the following (save to SOCIAL.md):
  (1) Twitter/X post — under 280 chars
      Show something CONCRETE (a feature, a metric, a before/after)
      One relevant hashtag. No hype words ('revolutionary', 'game-changing').
  (2) LinkedIn post — 3 paragraphs:
      Para 1: the problem that existed
      Para 2: what was built and how
      Para 3: what you learned or what it enables
      Conversational, no buzzwords, authentic.
  (3) Demo script — 3 bullet points for a 30-second screen recording
      Each bullet: what to show, what to say

Update session file:
done: wrote social content to SOCIAL.md
next: record demo video using the script
tests: n/a
todos: 0
health: good
continue: Resolve the pending question using available context and keep going. Follow CLAUDE.md. Do not stop to ask again. When done, update the session file with done/next/tests/todos/health lines.
